provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

examples.label: positive
negative

value.reason: The route GET /rest/user/authentication-details (server.ts:640) calls authenticatedUsers(), and that handler runs `UserModel.findAll()` (routes/authenticatedUsers.ts:12) with no where clause and no filter by the requesting user's id. The User model holds personal profile data: email, username, role, lastLoginIp, profileImage and other string fields. The route line shows no role check or ownership check, and the context marks the exposure as Public. So any caller who reaches the endpoint gets every user's account record, not just their own. This matches the positive SEC-07 example, which also lists all users with findAll and returns their dataValues. It does not match the negative example, which ties the query to the logged-in user. This is a failure to control access to personal data and to limit which object properties the API returns. The handler's response mapping is not shown, so it is not visible whether sensitive fields such as the password hash are masked. Even so, emails, roles and last-login IPs of all users would be exposed.
